primary_claim: Adding noise to activations/weights or using MELBO can increase how often an instruction-tuned LLM gives faithful, truthful, or non-sandbagged answers, but the same interventions barely help elicit hidden capability from a password-locked model, especially under RL.
contradicts_or_qualifies: Tice 2024 partially unlocked password-locked models by adding noise to weights, but using LLM-with-added-noise as an exploration policy during Math RL did not improve RL performance in this post's experiments
stated_future_work: explore intermediates between adding noise to a bias at layer 7 and adding noise to every weight in a network
explore using much more optimization power to find good noise vectors
explore techniques other than adding noise or using MELBO
explore ways to tune the level of noise more intelligently
explore using certain easy prompts where it is easier to elicit the desired behavior as a stepping stone towards harder ones
limitations_stated: results from previous work and the present results are lukewarm
not rarely able to find a vector that recovers entirely a hidden behavior
situation seems especially dire for eliciting complex many-token behaviors
chlorine gas elicitation result is not very conclusive since the rate the model is helpful is already quite high without intervention
adding noise is surprisingly ineffective for improving RL exploration on the password-locked model
quote: Adding noise or using MELBO can increase the frequency at which models give faithful answers.
